title: Delhivery shares gain 6% after Q2 results, JPMorgan, Jefferies, Kotak, Citi maintain buy calls - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Delhivery shares settled 6 per cent higher on Monday following the company’s Q2FY27 results, with brokerages highlighting improved margins, higher yields and growth in express parcel volumes. The company reported standalone profit after tax (PAT) of ₹66.7 crore in the September 2026 quarter, compared with ₹78.2 crore in the June 2026 quarter and ₹58.4 crore in Q2FY26.

The stock ended 5.89 per cent positive at ₹408.75 on the NSE after rising to ₹423 from ₹386 previous close.

The company’s board also approved an investment of up to ₹36 crore in Delhivery Fintech Distribution Private Limited (DFDPL), a wholly owned subsidiary, in one or more tranches.

According to JPMorgan, Delhivery’s Q2 revenue grew 20 per cent y-o-y to ₹30.7 billion, while reported EBITDA increased 37 per cent to ₹2.05 billion.

Express parcel volumes grew 32 per cent y-o-y, while the part-truckload (PTL) EBITDA margin improved to 12.8 per cent.

Kotak said reported EBITDA grew 29 per cent y-o-y, beating its estimates by 16 per cent, supported by improved service margins. Express parcel yields improved, while PTL and supply-chain services supported profitability.

Kotak also noted that working capital declined to five days of sales, while flagging Meesho insourcing as a key risk.

JPMorgan maintained its overweight rating on Delhivery with a target price of ₹590. The brokerage raised its FY27 EPS estimate by 10.9 per cent and expects adjusted EBITDA margins to improve sharply in the second half.

Jefferies maintained its buy recommendation but cut its target price to ₹470 from ₹540. The brokerage said adjusted EBITDA beat estimates despite the deferred festive season, with margin expansion supported by price hikes and operating leverage.

Jefferies added that express parcel growth benefited from lower Meesho insourcing and new initiatives. Sequential realisations improved after six quarters of decline, while PTL momentum remained healthy. However, rising Meesho insourcing remains a key medium-term risk.

Kotak maintained its buy rating and retained its fair value at ₹550. The brokerage highlighted improving express parcel yields and profitability support from PTL and supply-chain services.

Citi maintained its buy recommendation but lowered its target price to ₹545 from ₹570. The brokerage said margins beat estimates despite softer volumes, supported by higher yields, inflation pass-through and an improved shipment mix.

Citi noted that industry consolidation had improved the pricing environment and D2C volumes remained strong despite broader industry headwinds. It added that automation, robotics and AI investments should support operating leverage. However, the brokerage cut adjusted EBITDA estimates due to higher growth investments and corporate overheads.
